workarounds.symptom: generate-cli: generated CLI raises JSONDecodeError on any optional string parameter
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Accept plain values for optional parameters in generated CLIs. Target files: fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/cli/generate.py, tests/cli/test_generate_cli_arguments.py, docs/cli/generate-cli.mdx. Pydantic describes `greeting: str | None = None` as `anyOf: [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}]`, but `generate-cli` only recognized unions written as a `type` list. Every optional parameter therefore took the complex-type path: the generated command ran `json.loads()` on the value and dumped the JSON Schema into `--help`, so `--greeting H... (Ref: https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/6106)

workarounds.symptom: Client hydration fails for JSON Schema references into arrays
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Resolve JSON Schema references through arrays. Target files: fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/utilities/json_schema_type.py, tests/utilities/json_schema_type/test_array_references.py. When schema dereferencing is disabled, a tool can return valid structured content while the client leaves `result.data` as `None`. A reference such as `#/properties/template/anyOf/0` reaches an array, but the resolver calls `.get()` on it instead of selecting an element. (Ref: https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/6098)

workarounds.symptom: ctx.elicit() rejects a response model with an optional field (`X | None = None`)
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Accept optional fields in elicitation schemas. Target files: fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/client/elicitation.py, fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/server/elicitation.py, tests/client/test_elicitation.py. `ctx.elicit()` builds the form schema with `ElicitationJsonSchema`, and Pydantic renders a field typed `str | None = None` as `anyOf: [{type: string}, {type: null}]`. The validator's union branch rejects the `null` member, so a response model with an ordinary optional field raises `TypeError` and the tool call fails. The MCP elicitation primit... (Ref: https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/5907)

workarounds.symptom: ctx.report_progress() fails a task=True tool when total is 0
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Skip the Docket total update when report_progress total is below 1. Target files: fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/server/context.py, tests/tasks/server/test_context_background_task.py. In a background task, `Context.report_progress()` hands `int(total)` to Docket's `ExecutionProgress.set_total()`, which raises `ValueError("Total must be at least 1")` for anything below 1. Only `LookupError` is caught there, so the error fails the task. A `task=True` tool that follows the progress docs (`total=len(items)`) therefore works for every ba... (Ref: https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/5905)

Fix: Accept the tool name as the first argument of `call --command`. Target files: fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/cli/client.py, tests/cli/test_client_commands.py. `fastmcp call` takes the server spec as its first positional argument, followed by the target and any `key=value` arguments. When `--command` supplies the server instead, there is no spec to pass, so the parser still binds the first positional (the tool name) to `server_spec` and the first `key=value` to `target`. The result is that `fastmcp call --command 'npx -y @mcp/server'... (Ref: https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/5883)

workarounds.symptom: Resource template parameters skip int/float/bool coercion under from __future__ import annotations
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(resources): coerce template parameters from resolved hints. Target files: fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/resources/template.py, tests/resources/test_resource_template_query_params.py. Under `from __future__ import annotations`, `FunctionResourceTemplate.read()` saw string annotations, skipped its `int`/`float`/`bool` coercion and left the value to pydantic, so a postponed-annotation template accepted `on`/`off`/`t`/`y` for `bool` (rejected since #3434) and `1.0` for `int`. (Ref: https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/6471)

workarounds.workaround: Fix: Stop the SSE endpoint sending a second response after its stream. (Ref: https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/6431)

workarounds.symptom: `StdioTransport(keep_alive=True)` can't be reused across concurrently-alive event loops — `initialize` handshake hangs for the full `init_timeout`
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Reconnect StdioTransport when reused on a different event loop. Target files: fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/client/transports/stdio.py, tests/client/test_stdio.py, docs/clients/transports.mdx. a kept-alive stdio session belongs to the event loop that created it. reusing the same `Client` from a second loop handed that loop the first loop's session. its responses never arrived, so `async with client` hung forever, and `init_timeout` didn't bound it. (Ref: https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/6425)

workarounds.symptom: `logging/setLevel` is ignored for `ctx.log()` calls from tools of a mounted server
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Apply logging/setLevel to mounted servers over HTTP sessions.
